jobs.name: Calendar Sync — Morning (7 AM MST)
jobs.prompt:
You are running the Google Calendar → Obsidian sync script. Your job is to:

1. Run the calendar sync script
2. Report back what events were found

The script is at: C:/Users/sbrooksby/AppData/Local/hermes/profiles/paul/scripts/calendar-sync.py

Run it like this:
python3 "C:/Users/sbrooksby/AppData/Local/hermes/profiles/paul/scripts/calendar-sync.py"

The script will:
- Fetch today's events from Google Calendar
- Write them to Admin/Google-Calendar/YYYY-MM-DD.md (in the Team-Brain vault at C:/Users/sbrooksby/Downloads/Team-Brain/)
- Write upcoming events to Admin/Google-Calendar/Upcoming.md
- Print a summary to stdout

If the script fails because credentials.json or token.json is missing, note that in your response and stop — do NOT try to fix it. The user needs to set up Google OAuth first (see Admin/Google-Calendar-Setup.md for instructions).

If the script runs successfully, report:
- How many events were found today
- What those events are (title, time, location, link)
- Any upcoming events beyond today

Keep your response concise — focus on the events found. This is a morning sync (7 AM MST) so focus on today's meetings and what the user should be aware of.

jobs.name: End-of-day work log — Team-Brain daily note
jobs.prompt:
You are doing an end-of-day log compilation for Seven Brooksby's Team-Brain vault.

VAULT: C:\Users\sbrooksby\Downloads\Team-Brain

TODAY: Compute today's date. Construct the daily note filename: YYYY-MM-DD - WeekdayName.md (e.g., 2026-09-30 - Wednesday.md). Path: VAULT/Daily/<filename>. Skip if today is Saturday or Sunday.

Tasks:
1. Read today's daily note.
2. Check Master-Dashboard/Action Items.md — find items marked [x] that reference today's date (look for "Sep 30", "9/30", "today", or today's numeric date).
3. Check Master-Dashboard/Pulse.md for today's updates.
4. Use terminal to find markdown files modified today in the vault:
   cd /c/Users/sbrooksby/Downloads/Team-Brain && find . -name '*.md' -mmin -720 -type f
   Focus on new/changed files in: Daily/, Meetings/, Team-Profiles/, Projects/, Master-Dashboard/.
5. For any new meeting notes created today, read them and extract key accomplishments.
6. Compile a "Work Completed with Paul" section. Replace any existing "Work Completed with Paul" section in the daily note. Format as a bulleted list:
   ## Work Completed with Paul
   - [done] Concrete item description
   - [done] Concrete item description
   ...
   If nothing was found, write:
   ## Work Completed with Paul
   - No work logged today yet.

7. Update the "Last updated" line at the bottom of the daily note to today's date.
8. Report to the user what you wrote (this gets delivered via Telegram).

Be thorough. Check action items, pulse, meetings, profiles, and project files. Write concrete items, not vague summaries.

jobs.name: Weekly Briefing refresh — Mondays 7 AM
jobs.prompt:
You are generating Seven Brooksby's Monday morning Weekly Briefing for his Team-Brain vault.

VAULT: C:\Users\sbrooksby\Downloads\Team-Brain

TODAY: Compute today's date. If today is NOT a Monday, respond with exactly "[SILENT]" and stop.

TASKS:
1. Read every file in VAULT/Daily/ for the PREVIOUS week (the 7 days before today, weekdays only). Skip Sat/Sun — the user does not work weekends.
2. Read VAULT/Master-Dashboard/Action Items.md — pull open items, group by overdue / this week / upcoming.
3. Read VAULT/Master-Dashboard/Pulse.md for current team status and open promises.
4. Read VAULT/Admin/Google-Calendar/{today}.md and VAULT/Admin/Google-Calendar/Upcoming.md for today's meetings and the week ahead.
5. Read the Team-Profiles/ files for anyone with an open commitment.

THEN write a NEW Weekly Briefing to VAULT/Master-Dashboard/Weekly Briefing.md containing:
- Title: "# Weekly Briefing — Week of <Month D, YYYY>"
- A "Read This First" section: the single biggest tension or risk for the week. Two competing facts count more than a list.
- "Last Week at a Glance": what got done, big themes, what is still hanging.
- "Today's Schedule": from the calendar file, as a time table.
- "Week Ahead": meetings and 1-on-1s, including whether recurring invites exist.
- "Focus for the Week": 2-3 items max, ordered by leverage. Say plainly which is the one to do.
- "People": one line per person with an open item — what to remember before talking to them.
- "Carried-Over Debt": a table of stale items with how long they've been sitting.
- "Notes for the Week": empty space for the user.

STYLE RULES:
- Concrete, not vague. Reference actual names, dates, numbers.
- Call out anything overdue or blocked on someone else.
- Flag when two things are in tension rather than listing them as separate tasks.
- Do not invent items. If the calendar is empty for a day, say to check it.
- Replace the file entirely — it is regenerated each week.

FINAL RESPONSE (delivered to Telegram): a 10-line summary of the week's top 3 priorities and anything overdue. No preamble.
